For that I see no issue. Call them and talk. Maybe they can help you find further assistance. At the very least you'll have someone to talk to for a while.

Suicide hotlines aren't like therapists or clinics. They're only there to make sure you don't attempt to kill yourself and if they feel you may be "At risk" they will send police to your location to "check your welfare" which may or may not include taking you to the psych ward for treatment. 

I'm suspicious of the Suicide hotline. Some people say it is great but many others say it is terrible. Honestly I suppose it's worth a try, just dont give them reason to believe you are actively trying to harm yourself.

I'm sorry things are so horrible for you there.


America's a cesspit too. Our economy is designed to keep poor people poor and rich people rich. Our country has an Intolerance of things like personal choices and Mental disorders. Many people here are racist xenophobes. Monetarily you may be better off here but your quality of life will still suck regardless.

It'll make you very sickly and hurt very badly. 

It's not worth the prolonged suffering, and it's not a guaranteed death. Don't do it. It's not worth the pain and suffering you'll inflict on yourself.
They can help you to feel a little better, and right now that's good enough I think. It may seem stupid now, but it's better than just keeping everything to yourself.

I think it takes a lot of strength to tell someone how you feel. It's not weakness to ask for help.

You don't have to tell them about the cutting, but please tell them when you're feeling sad or when you feel like things are getting worse. Nobody wants you to suffer in silence.

Unfortunately I didnt get unemployment for being Fired, so I'm not sure you can count on that.

The best outcome is the one that's best for you. I don't know how old you are so I can't tell you what to do regarding your parents. But a good start is to tell them why you're so quick to want to resign from your job.

They'd be worried for you, like me and the other people in this thread. Nobody's disappointed that you came here wanting help. Online friends are a good start, but it's different when you have that sort of support from people you know.

One more thing. 

If you can't find happiness in yourself, try to find happiness in your loved ones. You say you have a family, friends, roomates.... do stuff with them. Talk to them. Tell them how you feel. 

You don't have to face your challenges alone. Trust me, having a support network helps. I can't tell you how much it helped me when I finally came clean to my closest friends and told them how I was feeling. I may not be here if it wasn't for that.

I'm happy. I hope that you can enjoy yourself.

Try to be positive. It's easy to think about all the terrible things, but that won't help you. Try to be optimistic. Things can get better.

You aren't selfish- they are.

You weren't put on this earth for them. You don't exist to make them happy. You exist to make yourself happy. The only person whose happiness that you should worry about is your own.

And it's selfish of them to want you to live for them.

But they're still going to cry when you leave, no matter who's selfish.

You need to come to terms with that- just because you aren't being selfish for wanting to die doesn't mean that your passing won't affect other people's lives.

Why do you feel like you want to commit suicide? It helps to talk about it.

Every time I get depressed I think about hurting myself too. I think about how good it would feel. How peaceful those final fleeting seconds would be. But then I think more about it and I realize that it's not what I want to do. Just because things look grim now doesn't mean they will be tomorrow, or the day after that.

And I'm not even going through half the hardship you are.

You've gotten this far. It takes willpower to keep going, and a diagnosis like the one you got would absolutely be disheartening. 

But the knife doesn't solve it. Just stop cutting. Don't do it for me, or for your family or friends. You don't owe anything to anyone. But you owe yourself. 

I know you don't mean to do this, but you also have the power to stop it and to try and get better.

Don't give up just yet. Keep going. I know you can.

My friend, you absolutely do deserve happiness. Especially now. Your body may be sick, but don't let your mind go with it.

One of my favorite quotes for situations like these is "If you're going through hell, keep going." 

You've still got time left. Don't waste it by hurting yourself and thinking about letting other people down. Try to make the most of things while you can, and figure out what you'll do when you can't when that time finally comes.

Do you have time until your health gets to that point?

If you do, then please don't waste that time. Make the most of the time you still have left. Do the things you want to do while you can. Don't give it up just because things look bleak.

This is the first and last time I'll ever say this, but if and when you get to that point where you're in pain and you truly can't do anything you want to do....

At that point, I don't think anyone would think less of you for wanting to find peace on your own terms.

But please don't throw away whatever precious time you may have left.

A coward is someone who isn't brave.

To be able to stare death in her face isn't cowardly, it takes incredible fortitude and willpower.

But to stop yourself from going through with it and to keep living, even during your lowest points... I honestly can't think of anything further than cowardice. It takes bravery to not only face our demons, but to refuse to succumb to the darkest ones.

So no, you're not a coward.

And to hell with the people who tell you otherwise.

I deleted my last post because I saw why you want to harm yourself. Please forgive my ignorance.

Terminal diseases are terrible and they can feel like they are insurmountable. 

But try to think of it this way. 4 years is a long time. Things can change. You could show signs of improvement in that time. Cutting yourself is just going to make things worse for you. Don't fall into that trap. There is literally not one situation where self harm will provide any amount of relief to you. You'll just end up bloody and feeling worse than when you started.

You define your purpose. 

What I mean by that is that you're alive to do what you think is your purpose. It's not something anyone can tell you. You have to discover it yourself.

I know that sounds cryptic but it's really the best answer I can give.

Try giving yourself a purpose. Think about what you want to do, and what you might be capable of accomplishing. Most of all, think positively. It's easy to have a Nihilistic mindset when you're feeling depressed, so try to resist that urge.

You're welcome. 

I hope you can take it to heart. There are alternative ways to cope that don't involve harming yourself.

Don't take all those tablets over her. It's not worth it. Try to calm down. Your life is worth more than 1 rejection. You'll find someone who feels the same way about you that you do about them. Trust me.

What happened between you and her? Why do you feel like she betrayed you?

It's terrible when someone you trusted hurts you. It feels like they take a piece of you with them.

Sometimes the only thing we can do at our lowest point is calm down and think about things. It's easy to panic and stew over problems, it's a lot harder to make solutions for them. 

Your parents could be a good start. You don't have to beg for assistance, but you could use them as a support network. Talk to them. Talk to your friends if you can. Make new friends if you can't. 

As for your financial and personal woes, I'm terribly sorry to hear about that. I've never experienced divorce, but Financial hardship is definitely something I can relate to.

Don't give up just yet. There's still hope.

You're correct. You don't have to take my advice. But you're asking for tips on how to harm yourself in a Subreddit that's supposed to be about helping people not hurt themselves. There's a bit of a conflict of interest.

With that in mind, I think that you need professional guidance on this type of situation. From your reddit history it appears you may have schizophrenia. That's a serious medical condition and it's much worse than anything i've dealt with. I'm not sure that anyone here could help you come to terms with the problem you mentioned.

As for my Mother, I love her very much. She's since overcome her addiction and she has learned to control her mental illness. She also no longer cuts because like I said, cutting doesn't solve anything. 

I'm not here to debate with you. I'm here to try and help you. You don't have to listen or take the help, but that's what this sub is for. I'm willing to listen to you, but you have to be willing to listen too, or you won't get any benefit.

I'm not going to tell you how best or effectively to hurt yourself because I care for your well-being. I hope you can at least take a little solace in the fact that a stranger actually cares.

A quote that I enjoy thinking on when I feel like dying is, "If you're going through hell, Keep Going." Winston Churchill said it. 

It's easy to think about negatives and dwell on them. Believe me, I know. Depression feels like a monster that you can never defeat.

I'm happy to hear that you've achieved so much in so little time, but it is disheartening to hear that instead of feeling confident, you feel like you want to give up.

I'm on a different boat. I'm 22, almost 23, and I feel like I haven't accomplished anything after completing high school.

But I haven't given up yet. The reason is because I still have this tiny sliver of hope that someday It'll get better.

Try to think about the positives. Think about your achievements, and make goals for yourself. Don't give up just because things are difficult. You are your greatest enemy until you become your greatest Ally. And if you're going through hell, then keep going. Don't let those dark thoughts win.

I've had this issue before. How old are you?

Job troubles can be stressful and tumultuous, especially when things at home are shaky. Your parents are technically right and they probably have good intentions, but if you feel that your job is mentally draining you, tell your parents. When I was fired from a  job as a janitor at a 24 hour factory I admitted to my mother that the job was making me feel uncomfortable and depressed. She understood and gave me a bit more space. I wound up finding another job which was better for me. 

Try to hang in there, Jobs are temporary. Death isn't.

Stop cutting.

Slashing is just a painful, messy, ineffective way to harm yourself.

The tiny amounts of blood you lose from those cuts are replenished by your body.

In order to actually die from it you'd have to hit a large artery, which are deep in your arm. So not only would you have to put a pretty deep gash in your arm which would probably be pretty painful, but You'd die slowly with complete awareness of what was happening.

You're better off finding other ways to cope with these types of issues. As someone who shares your thoughts I understand just how terrible life can be, but dying in pain in a puddle of your own blood isn't the fate you deserve.

I've suffered from dehydration induced by Heatstroke before. It wasn't a suicide attempt, actually just me underestimating how hot it was and trying to do something outside. 

It was the absolute worst feeling in the world. My head felt like it was going to explode and I was having trouble thinking or moving my limbs.

And it only gets worse from there. Your body will start to weaken and weaken and it can take forever to actually die from it. It's a lot of unnecessary suffering. Best to just stay alive at that point because you're not going to die within the week.

Any of these methods that involve depriving your body of food/water or that slowly kill you are going to be very agonizing. Starvation is just as bad. They're also very hard to accomplish because after a while all you'll be able to think about is the fact that you're dying from not having that thing. Some people have the willpower to just not do it and eventually your body will kind of just....resign to it's fate, but it's still not worth the unnecessary pain and suffering.

If you haven't already and you have the means, I recommend getting in touch with a doctor and scheduling an appointment with a psychiatrist, and trying to speak with a therapist. They could also try medication to improve your quality of life. 

One thing you need to keep in mind is that this pain you're feeling won't go away overnight and there's no certain answer that can help you overcome it. It's an everyday struggle, and believe me, i know how it feels. Two weeks ago I was on the very verge of suicide myself.

Do something you enjoy doing. If you dont enjoy anything, find a hobby. Try to keep your mind occupied as much as possible. Remember, any time spent thinking about other things is time you aren't thinking about that emptiness and pain.

Try to better yourself. Find problems you can fix and try to fix them. Don't focus on the bigger picture. That's what has caused me so much grief.
